classification: GitLab CLI issue and merge-request link parsing and slot semantics
rationale: Retain all 12 original declarations and 15 explicit parameter rows. These call actual public parsing paths with independent values, distinct issue/MR namespaces, self-hosted subgroup URLs, null/create semantics and malformed/overflow rejection; they do not mirror a copied policy inventory.

cases.title: leaves the slot alone when the flag is absent
cases.reason: Absent issue and MR flags must preserve existing slots with undefined, independently of null clearing.

cases.title: reads the issue reference %s
cases.reason: All three bare, prefixed and padded issue references must normalize to their independently supplied positive integer.

cases.title: reads the merge request reference %s
cases.reason: Both bare and exclamation-prefixed MR references must use the separate merge-request namespace.

cases.title: reads a self-hosted issue URL, including a subgroup path
cases.reason: A real self-hosted subgroup issue URL must retain its issue number through the public CLI flag parser.

cases.title: reads a merge request URL with trailing segments
cases.reason: A merge-request URL with trailing diff segments must retain its MR number.

cases.title: refuses a merge request reference in the issue flag
cases.reason: Both wrong-prefix and actual MR URL inputs must be refused in the issue slot with issue-specific guidance.

cases.title: refuses an issue reference in the merge request flag
cases.reason: Both wrong-prefix and actual issue URL inputs must be refused in the MR slot with MR-specific guidance.

cases.title: clears the slot on set, and refuses to on create
cases.reason: Set may clear either namespace with case-insensitive null; create must refuse clearing with omission guidance.

cases.title: reports a flag given without a value
cases.reason: A bare boolean flag must fail as a missing value rather than becoming an ID.

cases.title: refuses %s
cases.reason: All eight empty, whitespace, zero, negative, malformed, foreign-key and nonnumeric URL inputs remain actual rejection controls.

cases.title: refuses the non-GitLab URL shape %s
cases.reason: Both missing GitLab separators and missing grouped project paths must reject, preserving malformed URL fallback protection.

cases.title: refuses a number too large to be an integer
cases.reason: A 400-digit input must reject instead of becoming Infinity or a persisted JSON null.

classification: SSH and paired-server selector discovery, ambiguity and mixed-version recovery
rationale: Retain all 19 declarations. Checked RuntimeClient spies and existing full RPC fixtures replace structural casts; retain independent target identities and guidance while requiring actual error codes and strict admission of legacy fallback only after method_not_found.

cases.title: matches the human label as well as the generated id
cases.reason: Label, exact generated ID and mixed-case name must all resolve the independently supplied target row.

cases.title: does not invent a match
cases.reason: An unknown target label must remain unmatched rather than guessing the only known target.

cases.title: matches a paired server by name or id
cases.reason: Paired server names and IDs must resolve on their own axis.

cases.title: points an SSH name at the SSH flag when a server was asked for
cases.reason: An SSH label requested as an environment must produce the actionable host flag and identify the SSH kind.

cases.title: points a server name at --environment when an SSH target was asked for
cases.reason: A server name requested as SSH must produce its environment flag and identify the paired-server kind.

cases.title: says nothing when the name exists on neither axis
cases.reason: A name absent from both axes must produce no speculative recommendation.

cases.title: does not suggest the axis that was already requested
cases.reason: Already requested SSH and environment axes must not produce redundant recommendations.

cases.title: resolves a label to the target id
cases.reason: Retain label-to-target resolution through actual list handling using a checked RuntimeClient spy instead of a structural cast.

cases.title: rejects an unknown target instead of letting it filter to nothing
cases.reason: Unknown SSH targets must retain independent message guidance and now require invalid_argument, preventing error-code regressions.

cases.title: names the paired server when an SSH target was asked for by a server name
cases.reason: A paired server used as SSH must retain actionable environment guidance and now require invalid_argument.

cases.title: says so plainly when the host has no SSH targets at all
cases.reason: An empty host target list must retain explicit no-target guidance and now require invalid_argument.

cases.title: falls back to the older listing when the newer method is absent
cases.reason: Legacy listing must retain target results, independently require summaries then listTargets then the matching target state call, and prove unavailable state does not erase a valid target. Sequential complete RPC fixtures replace permissive method branches.

cases.title: enriches legacy target rows from host-owned connection state
cases.reason: Legacy state enrichment must preserve exact win32, connected and connectionStatus projection and query the independently named target; use complete sequential RPC fixtures.

cases.title: returns nothing rather than masking the error it was enriching
cases.reason: A generic enumeration failure must preserve the original selector context by returning no alternatives and now require only the initial summary request, disallowing fallback on unrelated errors.

cases.title: refuses to guess between two ssh targets sharing a label
cases.reason: Two matching SSH labels must remain ambiguous and must not silently select a row.

cases.title: refuses to guess between two servers sharing a name
cases.reason: Two matching environment names must remain ambiguous and must not silently select a row.

cases.title: still resolves an exact id past a colliding label
cases.reason: Exact SSH and server IDs must resolve despite colliding human names.

cases.title: reports no ambiguity for a unique name
cases.reason: Unique labels on both axes must not report ambiguity.

cases.title: names both candidates when an ssh label is ambiguous
cases.reason: Ambiguous SSH resolution must keep both independent candidate IDs in recovery guidance and now require invalid_argument.
